headline: Jio lists today as markets open weak; L&T shines, GST rules ease

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning, and welcome to your Market Brief for Wednesday, the twenty-eighth of October.

Three things matter most today. First, Jio Platforms, India's biggest ever share sale, makes its stock market debut at ten this morning, with the grey market pointing to a healthy premium. Second, the market itself has opened on the back foot. The Sensex fell more than 650 points in the first minutes, as Brent crude climbed back towards 116 dollars a barrel after an attack on a Saudi refinery. And third, the US Federal Reserve announces its rate decision late tonight, Indian time, and that is keeping traders cautious around the world.

Along the way, we have strong numbers from Larsen and Toubro, a profit miss at Maruti Suzuki, and some welcome relief on GST that every accountant will want to hear about.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Yesterday was a session of big swings and no net movement. On monthly expiry day, the Sensex slipped just 8 points to close at 73,598, and the Nifty ended 3 points lower at 22,749. Selling in IT and the large private and public sector banks cancelled out gains elsewhere. State Bank of India, Axis Bank, TCS, Asian Paints, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the laggards, while Bharti Airtel, Trent, Maruti and Power Grid gained.

The real action was further down the market. The smallcap index jumped about two and a half percent, and the midcap index rose nearly one percent. Realty, pharma and auto shares led the sectors.

On flows, foreign institutional investors bought a net 4,240 crore rupees of shares, their biggest single day of buying this month. Domestic institutions sold about 1,250 crore rupees, ending a five-day buying streak.

This morning, though, the mood has soured. The Sensex opened about 667 points lower at 72,931, and the Nifty near 22,591. L&T jumped about six percent on its results, and Bajaj Auto, SBI Life and Maruti were also in the green. IT shares were the drag, led by Infosys, which drew four broker downgrades in a single day after it cut its sales outlook for this financial year.

The levels analysts are watching: Moneycontrol's trading plan sees support at 22,600 and then 22,400, with the Nifty needing to get back above 22,800 to head towards 23,000. Vinay Rajani of HDFC Securities says a sustained move above 22,800 could open the way to 23,175.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Jio is not the only debut today. Paras Healthcare also lists this morning. Its 1,450 crore rupee issue was made up of 500 crore rupees of new shares and 950 crore rupees sold by existing holders, at a price band of 660 to 693 rupees a share.

Opening today is MK Jewels, with a 275 crore rupee issue that closes on Friday, the thirtieth. It raised about 83 crore rupees from anchor investors, including Goldman Sachs.

And in the pre-listing market, a promoter of the IPO-bound Intellius Recode sold a 5.4 percent stake at 331 rupees a share, which values the company at around 480 crore rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results, and the star of the evening was Larsen and Toubro. Profit jumped 33 percent, and revenue rose 16 percent to about 78,750 crore rupees. Orders won in the September quarter came to nearly 1.48 lakh crore rupees, up 28 percent, and almost two-thirds of that came from overseas.

In autos, a tale of two companies. Maruti Suzuki sold a record 6.97 lakh vehicles in the quarter and lifted revenue 26 percent to about 53,355 crore rupees, with market share at 40.8 percent. But consolidated profit fell 26 percent to 2,466 crore rupees, missing expectations, as input costs rose and other income fell. Bajaj Auto, on the other hand, grew standalone profit 35 percent, on record revenue of about 20,003 crore rupees, powered by exports and a richer product mix.

Insurers had a good night. Star Health's profit more than tripled to 264 crore rupees, as its claims ratio improved to 69 percent. SBI Life grew profit 11 percent, with net premium income up about 8 percent. And Max Financial Services posted a profit of 100 crore rupees, against just 6 crore a year ago, with the value of new business up 21 percent in the first half.

On the weaker side, Adani-owned ACC saw profit slump 92 percent to 93 crore rupees on lower volumes. Vedanta Iron and Steel posted a loss of 324 crore rupees. AWL Agri Business saw profit dip 2 percent even as revenue rose 26 percent to 22,270 crore rupees. And Cipla's quarter was held back by a high base in its US business, though India sales held up. Hindustan Unilever reports later today.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
On the economy, the rupee is the story. It opened 9 paise stronger at about 95.03 to the dollar this morning. But the Reserve Bank is defending it partly by keeping cash tight in the banking system. Reuters, via the Economic Times, reports that banks' record cash surplus has faded, with the central bank capping its liquidity support at 1.5 lakh crore rupees, and overnight rates pushing towards the top of the policy band. Forex reserves fell about 5 billion dollars to around 721 billion dollars in the week to the sixteenth of October.

Not everyone likes that approach. Former governor Raghuram Rajan cautioned against defending the rupee at any cost, and said some weakness could even help exports.

On rates, Deutsche Bank expects the Reserve Bank to raise the repo rate to 6.25 percent by mid-2027, as inflation stays high. Icra expects bank credit growth to slow to 15 to 16 percent this financial year as rates harden. And Icra's chief economist Aditi Nayar estimates the West Asia crisis may cost the government around 1.35 lakh crore rupees so far, though she still sees growth above 7 percent in the September quarter. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said growth would have topped 8 percent but for global shocks.

On trade, Piyush Goyal said India could gain an edge over rivals from the trade pact being negotiated with the US, and that talks with Chile are close to the finish line. The government is also looking at ways to make 100 critical imported inputs at home, and to simplify approvals for investment from neighbouring countries. Closer to the farm, wheat sowing has covered only 11,000 hectares so far, against 27,000 a year ago, after a weak monsoon.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil is back on the boil. Brent fell nearly 2 percent on Tuesday to about 114 dollars, as traders watched Iran peace talks. But it has climbed again this morning to around 115 to 116 dollars, after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia revived supply worries. American crude is above 101 dollars. Gold is holding above 4,000 dollars an ounce ahead of the Fed.

On Wall Street, technology shares led a rally on renewed excitement about artificial intelligence. The Nasdaq had its best day since the second of October, and a key chipmaker index rose 2.3 percent. Asian markets are higher this morning too. The big event is the Federal Reserve's decision, due late tonight our time. Investors are also watching exit polls from Israel's election for what they might mean for the West Asia conflict.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. It is listing day. Business Standard says the grey market has Jio trading about 22 percent above its issue price of 1,119 rupees, and Mint says market watchers see a gain of up to about 25 percent. Moneycontrol reports that bids for the issue topped 7 lakh crore rupees, and that Jio's market value could pass 10.3 lakh crore rupees. And Nomura has started coverage with a buy rating and a target of 1,340 rupees, nearly 20 percent above the issue price, pointing to tariff hikes and home broadband growth. The one worry is timing, with the wider market opening sharply lower this morning.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, and there is plenty on GST. From the first of November, businesses will no longer need a prior agreement to give post-sale discounts under GST, a change expected to help consumer goods and pharma companies and retailers. Provisional refunds for businesses with an inverted duty structure are also being speeded up.

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has also issued a set of clarifications. Applicants will no longer need an Udyam certificate for registration, and applications with Aadhaar authentication must be processed within seven working days. Officers cannot invoke the fraud or suppression provisions just because tax is unpaid or a mismatch is found. They need specific evidence of intent to evade, set out clearly in the show cause notice. And multi-year notices are to be split up. That should mean fewer arbitrary demands for your clients.

In insurance, the regulator's chairman, Ajay Seth, said dynamic pricing is unacceptable, and warned that high commissions paid to some digital platforms push up premiums. Business Standard flags rising stress in gold loans, with repayment delays growing and renewal rules tighter, and warns against using them to pay off other debt. And one caution for investors: Sebi has fined Taurian MPS, its directors and its merchant banker 18 lakh rupees for failing to disclose key facts in its IPO documents.

So, what to watch today. Jio's opening price at ten, against the 1,119 rupee issue price. Whether the Nifty can hold 22,600 with crude near 116 dollars. Hindustan Unilever's results this evening. And the Fed's decision tonight. That's your Market Brief. Have a good Wednesday.
